historicalReferences: Think back to Mario Andretti's historic victory here in 1977, the first and only time an American driver won a Formula 1 race on American soil.
Who can forget the dramatic 1983 CART race, where Mario Andretti and Al Unser Jr. collided on the last lap, handing the win to Mario's son, Michael?
Long Beach has seen its fair share of championship deciders, including the tense 1995 CART finale where Al Unser Jr. secured the title.
The late 80s and early 90s were dominated by the Penske-Mercedes cars, and Long Beach was often the scene of their dominance.
This circuit has hosted some of the greatest names in motorsport, from Fittipaldi and Lauda to Mansell and Villeneuve.
The 1986 CART race saw a spectacular airborne crash involving several cars on the start/finish straight – a stark reminder of the dangers of street racing.
Remember the fierce rivalry between the Andretti and Unser families? Long Beach was often the battleground for their intense duels.
Long Beach transitioned from Formula 1 to CART in 1984, marking a new era for motorsport in Southern California.
The iconic Shoreline Drive has been the scene of countless overtakes and daring maneuvers throughout the years.
The spirit of innovation and competition has always been strong here, with teams pushing the boundaries of technology to gain an edge on this challenging circuit.

strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this abrasive street circuit, especially with the high temperatures we're expecting today. Expect to see drivers managing their tires carefully.
The pit window here is relatively short, meaning teams will need to execute their stops flawlessly to avoid losing valuable time.
Fuel consumption is always a concern at Long Beach, as the stop-start nature of the circuit puts a strain on the fuel tanks.
Undercut or Overcut? With limited overtaking opportunities, the timing of the pit stops will be critical in determining the race outcome.
A safety car is almost a certainty at Long Beach, so teams will need to be prepared to react quickly to changing circumstances.
Track position is king here, making a good start and a clean first few laps absolutely essential.
The Historic layout's 3.251km distance makes fuel strategy slightly different than other configurations - every drop counts!
With limited run-off areas, any mistake can be costly, forcing teams to consider a more conservative strategy.
weatherCommentary: The California sun is beating down on Long Beach today, making it a hot and challenging race for both drivers and machines.
